entries.reason: The test is named 'REGRESSION: protective comment present'. Its subject IS the header banner explaining that deleting this route drops /rsvp/{id} into +not-found.tsx (the white screen of ORCH-1150 D-4). A banner lives in a comment by construction; the surrounding suite carries the behavioural assertions.

Same protective-banner class, on the RSVP preview route. The test is 'STATES + PROTECTIVE COMMENT: loading spinner shell + DO NOT delete header' and asserts Spinner and router.canGoBack() behaviourally in the same test; only the banner clause is comment-bound.

A strict-grep allowlist tag is DEFINED as a comment by this directory's README ('// orch-strict-grep-allow <gate-tag> — <reason>'). Asserting it can only ever match a comment. The same test asserts the wrong-wizard redirect behaviourally on the two lines above.

The test is named 'F-1 protective comment marker is present' and exists so a future author does not re-add router.replace because it 'feels right'. The no-navigation behaviour itself is asserted separately in the same file (the router dependency is proved absent from the deps array).
